newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger's parliament installed, transition ends.
newsitem.headline: Niger's parliament installed, transition ends.

text.p: A newly elected parliament in the West African state of Niger took office on Friday, ending a political transition launched by President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara's military coup last January, officials said.
A total of 80 legislators, elected on November 23 in polls boycotted by the opposition, took their seats.
A further three seats remain to be decided in by-elections on January 19.
Mainassara seized power last January 27, saying he wanted to end political deadlock between the then elected president, Mahamane Ousmane, and his prime minister, Hama Amadou.

He won presidential elections in July after scrapping the independent electoral commission in mid-poll. The opposition boycotted the November elections after failing to secure the scrapping of the July result.
The arid and impoverished nation's parliament is dominated by independents supporting Mainassara.
